enacted_status.reason: CR-098-2025's 180-day pause expired on its own term (2026-03-15) and Executive Order 1-2026's administrative hold ran through 2026-04-30 (and was further extended administratively through 2026-06-30 per Brandywine MD reporting). On 2026-07-07 the County Council adopted Resolution CR-066-2026, establishing a new, distinct two-year moratorium (through 2028, or until comprehensive zoning legislation) on accepting/processing/approving data-center permits and subdivision plans. This is a new instrument continuing the same policy of a legislative pause, not a permanent replacement ordinance, so 'extended' rather than 'replaced' or 'expired' best fits: the county has kept the development pause continuously in effect through successive administrative and legislative instruments.

evidence.title: CR-066-2026 (Draft No. 1), A Resolution Concerning Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers
evidence.supports: Establishes the file number, exact title, final action date (7/7/2026), passage, and the two-year duration on accepting/processing/approving preliminary plans of subdivision and detailed site plans/permits involving qualified data centers.
evidence.quote: A RESOLUTION CONCERNING TEMPORARY MORATORIUM ON DATA CENTERS for the purpose of establishing a two (2) year moratorium on the acceptance, processing, review, and approval of applications concerning preliminary plans of subdivision and detailed site plans that include qualified data center uses.

evidence.title: Prince George's County Council approves 2-year data center moratorium
evidence.supports: Vote date (2026-07-08 per publication, council action 2026-07-07) and vote tally (7 in favor, 1 abstention, 3 absent), and confirms the Executive's prior EO 'remains in place until Sept. 30' as a separate, supplementary track.
evidence.quote: County Executive Aisha Braveboy's existing moratorium 'remains in place until Sept. 30,' and the council resolution 'supplements' her prior moratorium on permit processing from September 2025.

evidence.title: Zoning legislation puts Prince George's data center moratorium in question
evidence.supports: Confirms that as of 2026-07-21, no comprehensive siting ordinance had passed; instead a new competing zoning bill (Fisher) was introduced that could open a path around the moratorium's own exception clause, and had not been enacted as of that date.
evidence.quote: Council member Wanika Fisher plans to introduce zoning legislation that would permit data centers in specific rural, agricultural, and residential zones... The moratorium includes a loophole: it allows data centers to proceed if the county council enacts placement and operational legislation.

decisions.notes: Some secondary reporting gives conflicting vote tallies (The Banner: 7-1 with 3 abstaining/absent; AFRO: 1 opposed with 3 abstaining) -- both agree only one member (Tim Adams) voted against. No county-issued follow-on Executive Order text was independently retrieved; the EO extension to 2026-06-30 rests on a real-estate-industry blog (brandywinemd.com) rather than a government source, so that specific sub-fact is weighted lower than the CR-066-2026 legistar record.

evidence.title: Data Center Study
evidence.publisher: Baltimore County Government, Department of Planning
evidence.supports: Confirms Bill 3-26 (adopted February 2026) remains the operative instrument and that the Planning Board's report process -- which controls when the moratorium can end early -- is still in progress as of the fetch date (2026-07-31): the report was introduced 2026-07-16, a public hearing is set for 2026-09-03, and a Board vote for 2026-09-17. Since the moratorium runs until the earlier of 2027-01-01 or 90 days after the Board submits its report, and the report has not yet been finalized/submitted, the moratorium remains active and unchanged.
evidence.quote: In February 2026, the Baltimore County Council passed Bill 3-26: Zoning Regulations-Data Center Study... the Board will hold a public hearing on the report on Thursday, September 3, and the Board will vote on the report on Thursday, September 17.

decisions.notes: Row is accurate as of 2026-07-31: the moratorium has not reached either end condition (calendar date 2027-01-01, or 90 days post-report-submission, since the report is not yet finalized). Draft report and Baltimore Sun coverage (2026-07-17, 'Baltimore County report on data centers urges strict limits') indicate the substantive direction of the eventual regulations but do not change the moratorium's current force.

evidence.title: Policies Against Data Center Expansions Exist Across the State of Maryland
evidence.supports: Identifies at least three distinct Maryland local actions -- Montgomery County, Frederick County, and Baltimore City -- that would otherwise be bundled into this aggregate meta-row.
evidence.quote: Montgomery County Council voted unanimously to pause data center permitting... Frederick County Council passed a Critical Digital Infrastructure Overlay Zone... Baltimore City Council sent Bill 26-0158, a one-year moratorium on data centers using 10 MW or more, to the Mayor for signature (2026-05-11).

decisions.notes: This row is an aggregate meta-row, not a single instrument, and per the assignment instructions it should not be forced into one outcome. During this pass we were able to identify and independently source three of the underlying actions with primary or near-primary evidence (Montgomery County Council press release, Frederick County civic alert, and one secondary source for Baltimore City); these are reported individually under new_candidates rather than folded into this row. We recommend the meta-row be decomposed into per-jurisdiction rows using those candidates plus any other unitemized actions (e.g., Howard, Anne Arundel, Charles counties) not yet independently verified in this pass. Outcome is marked unresolvable for the row as given because no single 'status' can honestly describe an aggregate of at least three separately-timed, separately-enacted local actions.
